metadata.document_title: ICMR National Guidelines for Clinical Management of Dengue Fever and Severe Dengue in India
metadata.issuing_body: ICMR Expert Group on Vector-Borne Diseases

sections.text: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection caused by four distinct serotypes of the dengue virus (DENV 1-4) transmitted predominantly by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. In India and endemic tropical countries, infection manifests in three clinical phases: 1. Febrile Phase (Days 1 to 3): Sudden onset of high-grade continuous fever (39-40 C) accompanied by retro-orbital headache, severe body aches ('breakbone fever'), facial flushing, and maculopapular rash; 2. Critical Phase (Days 3 to 7, coinciding with defervescence): Characterized by increased systemic capillary permeability leading to plasma leakage into pleural and peritoneal cavities, hemoconcentration, and thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 100,000/uL); 3. Convalescent / Recovery Phase: Reabsorption of extravasated fluid over 48-72 hours with stabilization of vitals.

sections.section_title: Clinical Warning Signs of Severe Dengue
sections.text: The critical phase corresponds to the timing of plasma leakage. Patients must be monitored closely for warning signs signaling transition to Severe Dengue (Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever / Dengue Shock Syndrome): 1. Severe persistent abdominal pain or tenderness; 2. Persistent vomiting (>= 3 episodes in 24 hours); 3. Mucosal bleeding (epistaxis, gingival bleeding, hematemesis, melena, or menorrhagia); 4. Clinical fluid accumulation (pleural effusion, ascites); 5. Lethargy, restlessness, or altered sensorium; 6. Hepatomegaly (> 2 cm below right costal margin); 7. Laboratory hemoconcentration: rapid rise in hematocrit (>= 20% elevation from baseline) concurrent with a rapid decline in platelet count.

sections.section_title: Fluid Management and Medication Safety Warnings
sections.text: Judicious intravenous fluid management is the cornerstone of clinical therapy during the critical plasma leakage phase. Isotonic crystalloids (Normal Saline 0.9% or Ringer's Lactate) are the fluid of choice, titrated to clinical response (target urine output >= 0.5 mL/kg/hour in adults, normal pulse pressure >= 20 mmHg). Overhydration must be strictly avoided to prevent pulmonary edema. Critical Medication Warning: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, and Mefenamic acid are STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in suspected or confirmed dengue fever due to platelet inhibition and aggravated risk of severe gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) at standard therapeutic doses (500-650 mg every 6 hours, maximum 3-4 g/day in adults) is the only recommended antipyretic.
